title: Edit second sign-in factor rule
purpose: Choose which accounts must have a second sign-in factor, with a reason.
summary: Choose which accounts must set up an authenticator app before they can work. Only the admin role can do this, with a reason.

tasks.title: Require a second factor
steps: Tick [[Every staff account]], roles under [[Staff with these roles]], or the other groups of accounts.
If [[Confirm it is you]] is shown, type what it asks for: [[Your password]], a code in [[Authenticator or recovery code]], or both.
Select [[Save changes]]. You return to Security settings.

tasks.title: Stop requiring it
steps: Clear the ticks, give a [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]].

good_to_know: The rule applies at each account's next sign-in. Sessions it did not cover at sign-in are not interrupted; a superuser can end a person's sessions in the admin console.
An account the rule covers without an authenticator app is sent to set one up after signing in and opens nothing else first.
Shared demonstration accounts cannot add one, so a rule covering them stops them working.
If someone saved the rule after you opened the form, your change is refused and what you chose stays. Reload and compare.
Saving asks you to confirm it is you (your password, a code, or both, as the page asks), unless you confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. Signing in does not count.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Only the admin role may open this form; other staff roles, client portal accounts and a superuser without the role are refused. It opens from Edit on the Second sign-in factor panel of Security settings, as a dialog or a full page, and returns there. Your role is checked again as your account stands when you save.

items.label: Every staff account
items.description: Every account that is not a client portal account, whatever its role, including accounts without a role.

items.label: Staff with these roles
items.description: Administrator, Supervisor, Client services, Account manager, Technical staff. A staff account holding a chosen role is covered. Administrators do the work of every role, so choosing any role also covers them.

items.label: Staff who can view patient information
items.description: Staff accounts granted Can view patient information, to the account itself or through any of its groups (a role group or another group), with or without a role.

items.label: Accounts that can open the admin console
items.description: Accounts with staff status in the admin console, superusers among them.

items.label: Reason
items.description: Required, up to 2,000 characters. Kept with the change in the history on Security settings.

items.label: Your password
items.description: Under Confirm it is you, after the reason, while saving asks for it, and shown when your account has a password: your own current password. The help under it says what saving asks for and that you are not asked again in this browser for 5 minutes. Left empty: Enter your password to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect password. Accepted, but the code is not: Enter your password again with the code (the page does not keep it).

items.label: Authenticator or recovery code
items.description: Under Confirm it is you, shown when your account has an authenticator app: a code from it, or one of your unused recovery codes, which is then used up. Left empty: Enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code, to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect code. The password is checked first; when it is not accepted, the code is not checked and can still be used.

items.label: Save changes
items.description: Once you have confirmed it is you (see Confirm it is you), saves the rule with an audit event naming you, the rule before and after, and your reason. Saving the same rule records nothing and shows No changes to save.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Returns to Security settings without saving.

sections.title: Confirm it is you
paragraphs: Saving asks you to confirm it is you, unless you already confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. The Confirm it is you section then follows Reason for the change, in the dialog or on the full page, and nothing is saved until what you type there is accepted. Signing in does not count: only confirming again does, and a new sign-in, even in the same browser, starts without one. Once you have confirmed, neither this form nor the other pages that ask (the session limits, and account administration for a superuser) ask again in this browser for 5 minutes. A form opened while you were confirmed and saved after the 5 minutes passed asks then.

Confirming on Confirm your password, or with a code before a change to your own two-factor settings, counts too, once every factor your account has was given there within the last 5 minutes: each counts for 5 minutes from when it was given, so the earlier one runs out first. A confirmation here counts for those pages as well. A new password, or a new or different authenticator app, on your account since you confirmed makes the next save ask again, for both. An account with neither a password nor an authenticator app cannot confirm, so it cannot save the rule until it sets a password.

When the confirmation is missing or not accepted, nothing is saved and no audit event is written; your ticks and reason stay in the form. A confirmation accepted while another field is refused is kept: the form shows that field's error without the section, and saving again within the 5 minutes does not ask.

A password or code not accepted is listed in your own Sign-in history as Re-authentication failed and counts toward the failed sign-in limit; an attempt that limit refuses is listed as Too many failed attempts. What you type under Confirm it is you is never stored, logged or put in an audit event.

items.label: Too many failed login attempts. Try again later.
items.description: The failed sign-in limit refused your password or code before checking it, after too many that were not accepted. Wait a few minutes, then try again.

items.label: Too many attempts to confirm it is you. Wait a minute, then try again.
items.description: Shown after 10 tries within a minute by your account (the Confirm your password pages count too). Nothing was checked, and the refusal is not listed in Sign-in history.

items.label: Your account has no password to confirm it is you, so this change cannot be saved. Set a password on Change password first.
items.description: Your account has neither a password nor an authenticator app, so it has nothing to confirm with. Set a password from Change password in the account menu, then save again.

items.label: Your sign-in factors changed, or your confirmation ran out, while this page was open. Confirm it is you again.
items.description: An authenticator app was added to or removed from your account, or your confirmation ran out, while your save was being checked. Nothing is saved. The section now asks for what your account has: fill it in and save again.

sections.title: Rules and states
paragraphs: Only active accounts are counted. An account is covered when any ticked part covers it. Nothing is required until the rule is first saved.

Whether the rule covers an account is decided when it signs in, from the account and the rule as they stand then, read together. A session it covers reaches only the setup pages while the account has no authenticator app and the rule, as it stands, still covers the account; recovery codes alone do not count. A session it did not cover at sign-in is not held until the account signs in again.

The form carries the revision of the rule it showed. A change saved by someone else in between refuses yours, keeps your choices and asks you to reload and compare. That is checked only once you have confirmed it is you.
Which accounts must have a second factor is the laboratory's decision. The application sets none by default.
